demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued growth of India's digital economy, increasing adoption of digital payments and expansion of merchant networks support demand for technology-enabled business support services
- Growth in digital transactions and merchant networks supports demand for merchant acquisition, customer onboarding, field support and business correspondence services
- Growth of e-commerce provides opportunities for retailer identification, onboarding, order processing and inventory-related support
- Increasing adoption of technology, automation and data-driven processes by businesses creates opportunities for technology-enabled service providers
- Operating entirely within India limits direct impact from global economic developments, though global conditions may indirectly influence client spending and technology adoption

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Changes in client business models, employment practices and strategies may encourage clients to undertake activities internally rather than outsourcing, affecting demand and business volumes in certain service categories.
- Changes in domestic and global economic conditions, inflationary pressures and geopolitical developments may influence client spending and business expansion; any slowdown may impact demand for BPO and merchant acquisition services.
- The BPO and business support services industry is competitive on quality, technology, pricing and service capabilities; increased competition may affect margins, client retention and the Company's ability to expand.
- Changes in laws relating to merchant onboarding, KYC requirements, data protection and employment practices may increase operational complexity and compliance costs; non-compliance may adversely affect operations and client relationships.
- Increasing reliance on technology and digital processes exposes the Company to system disruption, cybersecurity incidents, data privacy breaches and unauthorised access, which could disrupt service delivery and customer confidence.
- Changes in clients' business requirements, operating models or spending priorities may affect outsourced service volumes; reduction, termination or non-renewal of significant client engagements may impact business and financial performance.
- Service delivery depends on availability of skilled and trained personnel; employee attrition, recruitment and training challenges or operational disruptions may affect service quality and business continuity.
- Implementation and evolution of applicable Labour Codes and related rules may change employment practices, statutory obligations and compliance costs, impacting operating costs and HR management.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthening domestic market presence through long-term client relationships, quality service delivery and continuous operational improvements
- Enhancing service quality through technology adoption, process optimisation and skilled human resources
- Improving operational efficiency, strengthening technology capabilities, maintaining service quality and developing long-term client relationships
- Expanding service offerings across merchant acquisition, account management, field support, business correspondence, e-commerce solutions and technology development
- Concentrating resources within its single operating segment to optimise operational efficiencies and maintain a targeted approach toward market expansion and risk management
